newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: AMLC Beef Weekly - Australian export prices.
newsitem.headline: AMLC Beef Weekly - Australian export prices.

text.p: Corp's (AMLC) weekly export prices are as follows:
AUSTRALIAN EXPORT PRICES TO U.S. IN U.S. CENTS/LB, CIF.
Bull (95 Chemical Lean) 86 -6 on last week
AUSTRALIAN EXPORT PRICES TO JAPAN IN U.S. CENTS/LB CIF.
Chilled grassfed fullsets 124 +3 on last week
AMLC COMMENTARY: Australian cattle prices were generally firm to higher this week. Numbers increased in Queensland and New South Wales but were lower in Victoria.

It has been a very difficult week for imported meat traders in the U.S. market. U.S. domestic lean beef prices remained firm in response to spot buying for the 4th of July holiday, however, this demand largely bypassed imported product as end-users found they had sufficient imported beef inventories. A 3 USc/lb fall in imported (ex dock) prices has widened the
differential in favour of domestic prices to a massive 11 USc/lb.

As the U.S. cow kill slows through the U.S. summer, this differential generally moves in favour of U.S. product. This is because markets are generally well supplied with imported beef as a result fo the autumn-winter cow cull in the southern hemisphere. However, large differences have typically not persisted for long. Most market participants expect U.S. domestic prices to ease early next week as buying for the 4th of July holiday winds up.

Although price movements for U.S. and imported lean product have diverged this week, the close correlation that exists between the two should allow Australian producers to make use of the new 90CL boneless beef futures contract launched on the Chicago Mercantile Exchange (CME) this week.

Since 1996, the movement in U.S. lean beef prices have explained 84 percent of the movement in Australian manufacturing beef export prices. As manufacturing beef export prices are a major determinant of cow prices, it follows that Australian exporters or producers may be able to use this contract to protect or set the future prices of their beef exports or cows.

At least, this contract will provide a market reading on future movements in the prices of manufacturing beef in the U.S. market. Bearing in mind that, on the spot market, US 90CL beef traded at 99USc/lb this week, last night (Thursday US time) the August contract closed at 93USc/lb, October at 90.6USc/lb and December at 94USc/lb.
In Japan, export prices firmed slightly this week. Although the wet season has been rather mild this year, demand is perceived as being weak in comparison to previous seasons.
Although a fall in wholesale prices and a lift in export prices reduced the margin this week, there continues to be an unusually large disparity of 11 USc/lb between wholesale and export prices.
Historically, this margin has been much lower. A further tightening in this margin, through lower wholesale prices or higher export prices, would be to the benefit of Australian exporters.
